title: Isomer Stability of N24, N30, and N36 Cages: Cylindrical versus Spherical Structure
notes_general: All species are large three-coordinate all-single-bond nitrogen cages (analogous to fullerenes), described by point group + polygon composition (n3,n4,n5,n6 = number of 3/4/5/6-sided faces, satisfying Euler's theorem n3+n4+n5+n6=(x/2)+2 and 3n3+2n4+n5=12). NO numeric bond-length/angle table or figure labels are given anywhere in the paper -- structures are pure topology (point group + polygon spec) with relative energies only. All confirmed as minima at HF/CC-PVDZ (paper states this explicitly for the N24 set; implied for N30/N36 by 'results follow the corresponding results for N24'). These are all larger than any existing corpus entry (existing corpus tops out at N20) -- likely genuinely NEW sizes for the pool, though exact cage connectivity beyond the polygon count would need reconstruction via a fullerene-cage-generation tool (not just generic_guess) for a truly faithful geometry.

bond_params.shape: fullerene-like cage, polygon spec 00(12)2 (0 triangles, 0 squares, 12 pentagons, 2 hexagons)

species.notes: Reference isomer (0.0 kcal/mol) in Table 1-2, but NOT the most stable overall (2066P is ~100-110 kcal/mol more stable per MP4).

bond_params.shape: octahedral cage, polygon spec 0608 (0 triangles, 6 squares, 0 pentagons, 8 hexagons)

species.notes: Least stable N24 isomer studied, +200 to +206 kcal/mol above 00(12)2.

bond_params.shape: cylindrical cage, polygon spec 2066 (2 triangles surrounded by pentagons = 'caps', hexagonal tube between); 2 triangles, 0 squares, 6 pentagons, 6 hexagons

species.notes: MOST STABLE N24 isomer in this study (~100-110 kcal/mol more stable than 00(12)2 per MP4, all basis sets/methods agree on this ranking). Authors' key finding: triangles-surrounded-by-pentagons end-caps + hexagonal tube = most stable arrangement, more important than simply maximizing pentagon count.

bond_params.shape: same 2066 polygon spec as 2066P but triangles surrounded by HEXAGONS instead of pentagons

species.notes: Same polygon COUNT as 2066P but much less stable (+22 to +33 kcal/mol vs 00(12)2, vs -100 for 2066P) -- demonstrates it's the triangle/pentagon adjacency, not polygon count alone, that stabilizes.

bond_params.shape: polygon spec 0284 (0 triangles, 2 squares, 8 pentagons, 4 hexagons)

species.notes: -23 to -32 kcal/mol vs 00(12)2 (second most stable after 2066P).

bond_params.shape: polygon spec 400(10) (4 triangles, 0 squares, 0 pentagons, 10 hexagons)

species.notes: +7 to +29 kcal/mol vs 00(12)2, slightly less stable than reference.

bond_params.shape: cylindrical cage, polygon spec 2069 (2 triangles as end-cap pentagon-surrounded feature analogous to N24 2066P, hexagonal tube)

species.notes: MOST STABLE N30 isomer, ~100 kcal/mol (HF/MP4) / ~80 kcal/mol (B3LYP) more stable than the fullerene-like isomers below -- same cylindrical-cap pattern as N24 2066P.

bond_params.shape: fullerene-like cage, polygon spec 00(12)5, C2v variant #1

species.notes: +179.5 to +220.3 kcal/mol vs 2069 cylinder (least stable N30 isomer studied).
